questions.explanation:
(a) I, you and she
If two or more singular pronouns are used together, the correct
order is 231 according to the person they denote. Therefore, the
correct order for the given sentence is You(2nd person), she(3rd
person) and I(1st person). Hence, ‘You, she and I’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

options: as he took money from you many times
questions.explanation:
(b) five thousand rupees all together
‘All together’ must be replaced with ‘altogether’, which means
totally. Hence, ‘five thousand rupees altogether’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.explanation:
(b) on
‘On’ is used to indicate a specific occasion or day. ‘During’ is
used to indicate a specific period of time. Similarly, ‘pandemic’ is
a specific period of time. Hence, ‘during’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: In August, she will be / enjoying / all the fruits her
questions.explanation:
(a) will plant last January
The phrase ‘last January’ indicates the use of simple past tense.
‘Will plant’ must be replaced with the past form ‘planted’. Hence,
‘planted last January’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

‘Less’ must be replaced with ‘low’ as there is no comparison in
this sentence. Hence, ‘train accident is fairly low’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.explanation:
(b) worse
‘Worse’ must be replaced with ‘the worse’. When change in one
thing causes the change in the other and two comparative
degrees are used to indicate this relationship, it is called
successive comparison. Article ‘the’ is used before both the
comparative degrees. Hence, ‘the worse’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mr. Unkerton glanced / to the inspector, / who merely
questions.explanation:

antecedent. In the given sentence, ‘the book’ is the antecedent,
which will be used before ‘that’. Hence, and shouted, “Here lies
the book is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Raghu did not get the job / because he did not have /
options: Raghu did not get the job
questions.explanation:

‘Enough’ is an adjective which describes the noun ‘experience’,
therefore ‘enough’ will be used before ‘experience’. Hence,
‘enough experience for the job’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

options: I had been studying English for three years by the end of this
I have been studying English for three years by the end of this

I was studying English for three years by the end of this

given in option (c) is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

‘for’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: John is really / good in/ playing/ the piano.
questions.explanation:

The structure ‘good + at + V ’ is used to show that you are very
ing
skilful and clever at doing something. Hence, ‘good at’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The Supreme Court set away / the verdict of the High
options: and agreed to hear the plea
the verdict of the High Court
questions.explanation:
(b) The Supreme Court set away
‘Set away’ must be replaced with ‘set aside’. The phrasal verb
‘set aside’ means to deprive of legal effect because it has been
proved wrong. The given sentence states that the Supreme
Court set aside the verdict of the High Court. Hence, ‘The
Supreme Court set aside’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mrs. Premlatha asked / Malini to hand down / all the /
questions.explanation:
(c) Malini to hand down
‘Hand down’ must be replaced with ‘hand out’. The phrasal verb
‘hand out’ means to give a slip or document to someone. The
given sentence talks about giving all the payment slips. Hence,
‘Malini to hand out’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She is / as more intelligent as / her brothers are.
questions.explanation:
(d) as more intelligent as
‘As + adjective/adverb + as’ is a comparative structure in which
the adjective or the adverb is always in the positive degree.
Therefore, ‘more’ will be replaced with ‘much’. Hence, ‘as much
intelligent as’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He is waiting / at airport to receive / Mr. Smith, who is /
questions.explanation:
(d) at airport to receive
Article ‘the’ is used to refer to a specific or particular noun.
‘Airport’ given in the sentence is specific as the person is waiting
there. Hence, ‘at the airport to receive’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I hope that / yesterday's lunch / at Rahul's place / was at
questions.explanation:
(c) was at your liking
“To one’s liking” is the correct phrase, which means appealable
or enjoyable to someone. Therefore, ‘at your liking’ must be
replaced with ‘to your liking’. Hence, ‘was to your liking’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: She forbade / him not / to enter that / room.
questions.explanation:
(c) him not
‘Not’ must be removed from this sentence. ‘Forbade’ is the past
form of ‘forbid’, which means to not allow someone to do
something. The use of ‘not’ with ‘forbade’ is superfluous. Hence,
‘forbade him to’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He climbed of / the steep mountain trail, / his backpack
questions.explanation:
(d) He climbed of
‘Climbed of’ must be replaced with ‘climbed up’. ‘Up’ is used to
indicate upwards movement. Hence, ‘he climbed up’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Sam and Teena / had wondering / what to do this
questions.explanation:
(d) had wondering
The given sentence is an example of present continuous tense
and the subject ‘Sam and Teena’ is plural. ‘Plural Subject + are +
V ing ’ is the correct grammatical structure for it. Hence, ‘are
wondering’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: You know that I am fond of reading / and also that all
options: but you don’t know that this is one of
and also that all books are my favourite
You know that I am fond of reading
questions.explanation:
(c) my favourite book
‘One of + plural noun’ is the correct grammatical structure.
Therefore, the plural noun ‘books’ will be used. Hence, ‘my
favourite books’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.

A young boy offered her his seat.

I have a lot of work to complete.

life.
Article ‘an’ will be used before the noun ‘eraser’ as it starts with a
vowel sound. Hence, the correct sentence is- ‘I wish I had an
eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.’ (Correct)

questions.prompt: In addition with / the existing crisis in economy, / the
questions.explanation:
(d) in addition with
‘In addition to’ is the correct phrase. Hence, ‘in addition to’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

The train leaves the station at 8:00 a.m. every day.

questions.prompt: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft
An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft
questions.explanation:
(c) The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the
synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
‘Dance’ and ‘cleft’ mentioned in the sentence are specific and we
generally use the definite article ‘the’ before a specific or
particular noun. The noun ‘role’ is not specific and we generally
use an indefinite article before a non-specific noun. The word
‘crucial’ starts with a consonant sound, therefore, article ‘a’ will
be used before it. Hence, the sentence given in option (c) is
correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He will have to / knuckle up really seriously, / if he wants
questions.explanation:
(c) knuckle up really seriously
‘Knuckle up’ must be replaced with ‘knuckle down’. The phrasal
verb ‘knuckle down’ means to put in serious effort. The given
sentence states that he will have to knuckle down really
seriously if he wants to crack the upcoming deal. Hence,
‘knuckle down really seriously’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given
options: A lot of books and notes place in order look most
A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.
A lot of books and notes placed on order looks most
A lot of book and notes placed in order looks most
questions.explanation:
(b) A lot of books and notes placed in order look
fascinating.
‘A lot of books and notes’ is a plural subject that will take ‘look’
as a plural verb. The phrase ‘in order’ means arranged
systematically. We can not use the superlative degree of
‘fascinating’ as there is no comparison with any other thing.
Hence, the sentence given in option (b) is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He missed the college bus / because he woke up /
questions.explanation:
(d) unpardonably lately in the morning
‘Lately’ must be replaced with ‘late’. ‘Late’ means after the usual
or expected time. ‘Lately’ means in the recent times. The given
sentence is talking about waking up after the expected time in
the morning. Hence, ‘unpardonably late in the morning’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: After the match, / the stadium was the messiest / it’s
questions.explanation:
(a) No error
The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Gita got onto / the book / she was reading / this morning.
questions.explanation:
(c) Gita got onto
‘Got onto’ must be replaced with 'got into'. The phrasal verb ‘got
into’ means became interested in a subject or activity. The given
sentence talks about the interest of Gita in the book she was
reading. Hence, ‘Gita got into’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Although experts are worried / that retail inflation is
options: the crisis will soon blow away
questions.explanation:
(c) the crisis will soon blow away
‘Blow away’ must be replaced with ‘blow over’. The phrasal verb
‘blow over’ means to pass by or to end. The given sentence
states that the crisis will soon end. Hence, ‘the crisis will soon
blow over’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the option that has an error in the use of present
options: The painter is painting the wall right now.
The mother cooks delicious food for her children.
I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.
I have performed all my duties with utmost sincerity.
questions.explanation:
(c) 
I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.
Present perfect continuous tense will be used in this sentence
as a fixed period of time is mentioned with the preposition ‘for’.
Therefore, ‘am observing’ must be replaced with ‘have been
observing’. Hence, the correct sentence is - ‘I have been
observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.’ (Correct)

questions.prompt: My mother is 51 years old, / and my uncle is 48 years old.
options: and my uncle is 48 years old.
So my mother is old than my uncle
questions.explanation:
(c) So my mother is old than my uncle
‘Old’ must be replaced with the comparative degree ‘older’ as the
given sentence compares the age of mother and uncle. Hence,
‘So my mother is older than my uncle’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My sister is allergic with peanuts, so be cautious when
questions.explanation:
(c) allergic with peanuts
‘To’ is the fixed preposition used after the adjective ‘allergic’.
Hence, ‘allergic to peanuts’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: They have an information about the event.
The cat is sleeping on a mat.
She is an artist at a local gallery.
Can you bring me the keys to the car?
questions.explanation:
(a) They have an information about the event.
‘Information’ is an uncountable noun and we generally do not
use indefinite articles (a/an) with uncountable nouns. Therefore,
‘an’ will be removed. Hence, the correct sentence is- ‘They have
information about the event.’ (Correct)

questions.prompt: Whenever she is coming / here, she brings / many gifts
questions.explanation:
(c) Whenever she is coming
‘Whenever’ is used when one action is always followed by
another action. Simple present tense is used with ‘whenever’.
‘She’ is a singular subject that will take ‘comes’ as a singular
verb. Hence, ‘Whenever she comes’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given
options: She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes was
She was not allow to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were
questions.explanation:
(d) She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes
were dirty.
‘Singular Subject + was + V 3 ’ is the correct passive structure for
simple past tense. ‘Clothes’ is a plural subject that will take
‘were’ as a plural verb. Hence, the sentence given in option (d) is
correct. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My aunt came from Switzerland by the flight which was
questions.explanation:
(a) Switzerland by the
We generally do not use article ‘the’ after ‘by’ when we mention
the means of transport such as bus, train, bike, car, flight, etc.
Therefore, article ‘the’ will be removed. Hence, ‘Switzerland by’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: (1) We knocked across (2) early on Saturday (3) to enjoy
questions.explanation:
(d) We knocked across
‘Knocked across’ must be replaced with the phrasal verb
‘knocked off’. ‘Knock off’ means to stop work. The given
sentence states that we stopped work early on Saturday to enjoy
the beautiful weather. Hence, ‘We knocked off’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He bought strange vintage car on auction from the
questions.explanation:
(b) strange vintage car
We generally use an indefinite article (a/an) before a
non-specific noun. In the given sentence, the word ‘strange’
starts with a consonant sound. Therefore, article ‘a’ will be used.
Hence, ‘a strange vintage car’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I thought of this idea / just when you called / me

The given sentence is grammatically correct. (Correct)

The given sentence is grammatically correct (Correct)

questions.prompt: I are dancing with my husband at my sister’s wedding.
questions.explanation:
(d) I are dancing
‘Am’ is the correct helping verb to use with ‘I’ in present
continuous tense. Hence, ‘I am dancing’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: After the concert was over, / they go to a restaurant, /
questions.explanation:
(b) they go to a restaurant,
The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb
in the past form (V 2 ), not the present form (go). Hence, ‘they
went to a restaurant’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Renewable energy / sources like solar and wind power /
options: sources like solar and wind power
questions.explanation:
(c) will replaced traditional fossil fuels
‘Modal verbs’ are auxiliary verbs(also called helping verbs) like
can, will, could, shall, must, would, might, and should. However,
after a modal verb, we generally use the first form of the verb
(V ). Hence, ‘will replace(V ) traditional fossil fuels’ is the most
1 1
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Our family is planning / a trip to Europe next summer /
options: where we should visit several famous
a trip to Europe next summer
questions.explanation:
(a) where we should visit several famous
‘Should’ must be replaced with ‘will’ as the action of visiting
several famous landmarks will happen in the future (next
summer). Hence, ‘where we will visit several famous’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: It is he who work for the company for more than a
questions.explanation:
(b) who work
‘Who work’ must be replaced with ‘who has been working’ as we
use the perfect continuous tense with ‘for/since’ to indicate time
period. Hence, ‘who has been working’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The windows / violent banged / during the / storm
questions.explanation:
(d) violent banged
‘Violent’ must be replaced with ‘violently’ as the given sentence
needs an adverb to modify the verb ‘banged’. Hence, ‘violently
banged’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law / attended the
options: Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law
as his health is not more good
questions.explanation:
(d) as his health is not more good
‘More’ must be removed as we use comparative degree adjective
to make a comparison but there is no comparison between the
health of two people. The first part of the sentence is in the past
tense, so the verb in the second clause will also be in the past
tense(V 2 ). Hence, ‘as his health was not good’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Rahul thinks he is as smarter as his friends in the class.
questions.explanation:
(b) he is as smarter as
‘As + adjective/adverb + as’ is a comparative structure in which
we always use positive degree. Therefore, ‘smarter’ must be
replaced with ‘smart’. Hence, ‘he is as smart as’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Solutions to the country’s interior problems are still a
questions.explanation:
(d) the country’s interior
The correct word to use in this sentence is ‘internal’, not
‘interior’. ‘Internal’ means occurring inside a country. Hence, the
country’s internal is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
questions.explanation:
(a) They secret
The given sentence needs an adverb ‘secretly’ to modify the verb
‘decided’, not the noun ‘secret’. Hence, ‘They secretly’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He ran quick to catch the bus.
questions.explanation:
(d) quickly
The given sentence needs an adverb ‘quickly’ to modify the verb
‘ran’, not the adjective ‘quick’. Hence, ‘quickly’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The employees were comfortable / with me and they
options: I has worked there as a manager.
with me and they talked about

(a) I has worked there as a manager.
The given sentence is in the past tense, so it must have the verb
of past tense. ‘Had’ will be used instead of ‘has’. Hence, ‘I had
worked there as a manager’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four
questions.explanation:
(a) will pay dear
The given sentence needs an adverb ‘dearly’ to modify the verb
‘pay’, not the adjective ‘dear’. Hence, ‘will pay dearly’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: My brother received / his MBA degree into / the
questions.explanation:
(b) his MBA degree into
‘Into’ must be replaced with 'from' as we use ‘from’ to indicate
the source of something. Hence, ‘his MBA degree from’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He replied / in a dry tone, / “Ouch! I will not work / for
questions.explanation:
(d) ''Ouch! I will not work
‘Ouch!’ is used to express pain. However, in the given sentence,
the speaker replied in a dry tone. So, the correct interjection to
use is ‘Ugh!’. Hence, ‘Ugh! I will not work for you anymore’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mr. Surya / have no interior / motive in offering / you
questions.explanation:
(d) have no interior
‘Have no interior’ must be replaced with ‘has no ulterior’. ‘Mr.
Surya’ is a singular subject that will take ‘has’ as a singular verb.
Also, the correct word to use here is ‘ulterior’. ‘Ulterior motive’
means a secret reason for doing something. Hence, ‘has no
ulterior’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting
questions.explanation:
(a) I have the hundred reasons
The reasons given in the sentence are not specific and we use
indefinite article for a non-specific noun. Article ‘a’ will be used
as the word ‘hundred’ begins with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘I
have a hundred reasons’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined.
questions.explanation:
(b) had still overwhelmed
‘Had’ must be replaced with ‘were’ as the given sentence is an
example of a passive voice of simple past tense and ‘Plural
subject (they) + were + V ’ is the correct grammatical structure
3
for it. Hence, ‘were still overwhelmed(V )’ is the most

appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Due to the pandemic, / the prices of / medicines
questions.explanation:
(b) medicines increased
We use present continuous tense with ‘for/since’ to show that
something has been happening for a period of time. ‘Plural
subject (prices) + have been + V ing ’ is the correct grammatical
structure for it. Hence, ‘medicines have been increasing’ is the
most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The following sentence has been divided into four
questions.explanation:
(a) strengthen an intellectual
Indefinite article ‘a/an’ is not used for an abstract
noun(solidarity). The definite article ‘the’ is used before a
specific or particular noun. The given sentence is referring to a
specific type of solidarity. Hence, ‘strengthen the intellectual and
moral solidarity’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: It is said that Joseph was not ready to go to war.
Karl Marx was a renowned social scientist.
Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity.
It is impossible to wake Christine up in the morning.
questions.explanation:
(c) Indian force are known for their loyalty and integrity.
‘Forces’ will be used instead of ‘force’ according to the plural
verb ‘are’ and the plural adjective ‘their’. Hence, the correct
sentence is: “Indian forces are known for their loyalty and
integrity.” (Correct)

questions.prompt: Brr, the city view from the Eiffel Tower is amazing !
questions.explanation:
(d) Brr
An interjection is a word or phrase used to express a sudden
feeling. ‘Brr’ is used to express the sensation of cold. ‘Wow’ is
used to express a sudden feeling of amazement. Hence, ‘Wow’
is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

Hence, ‘they ran fast’ is the most appropriate answer.

options: he lived by the same principals
questions.explanation:
(c) he lived by the same principals
‘Principals’ must be replaced with ‘principles’ as the given
sentence talks about a kind of belief or idea that guides you.
Hence, ‘he lived by the same principles’ is the most appropriate
answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: We were on the way/ to the party;/ suddenly, there/ will a
questions.explanation:
(c) will a heavy downpour.
The given sentence is in the past tense, not in the future tense,
so it must have the verb in the past form ‘was’, . Hence, ‘was a
heavy downpour’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He never talks / for anybody. / He is alone / all day.
questions.explanation:
(b) for anybody
‘To’ is used to denote the person to whom someone is talking.
Hence, ‘to anybody’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: The police told the agitators to back in, else they would
questions.explanation:
(c) the agitators to back in
‘Back out’ is the correct phrasal verb to use here. ‘Back out’
means to withdraw or decide not to do something that was
planned to do. Hence, ‘the agitators to back out’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: We took dinner in a Chinese restaurant and were amazed
questions.explanation:
(b) the interior of a restaurant
Article ‘the’ is used when we refer to the same noun again
because it becomes specific. Hence, ‘the interior of the
restaurant’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mr. Ali’s shop / is further to / the hospital.
questions.explanation:
(a) is further to
‘Farther than’ will be used instead of ‘further to’. ‘Further’ is used
for metaphorical distance where ‘farther’ is used for physical
distance. The given sentence is talking about the physical
distance between Mr. Ali’s shop and the hospital. Hence, ‘farther
than’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Select the option that corrects the error in the given
questions.explanation:
(d) well
The given sentence needs an adverb(well) to modify the verb
(sings) and not an adjective(good). Hence, ‘Rahul sings well’ is
the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: In some countries, you are not able to drink until you are
questions.explanation:
(b) able to drink
The correct word to use here is ‘allowed’ instead of ‘able’. The
given sentence states that you are not allowed to drink until you
are 21. Hence, ‘allowed to drink’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Two of the world’s / best forwards / has played alongside
questions.explanation:
(d) has played alongside
According to the “Subject-Verb Agreement Rule”, a plural subject
always takes a plural verb. In the given sentence, ‘Two of the
world’s best forwards’ is a plural subject that will take ‘have’ as a
plural verb. Hence, ‘have played alongside’ is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Ourselves should not boast of one’s knowledge.
questions.explanation:
(c) Ourselves
‘Ourselves’ must be replaced with 'We' as we use a subjective
case pronoun (I/we/you) as the subject of a sentence. Hence,
'We' is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: He always wants to be in the company of those who are
questions.explanation:
(a) superior than him.
There are some words that imply comparison but do not take
‘than’. Rather, ‘to’ is used with them. For example:- superior to,
inferior to, prior to, senior to, junior to, elder to, etc. Hence,
‘superior to him’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: I have sing ‘Let It Go’ before a crowd of thousands of
questions.explanation:
(c) I have sing
With ‘has/have/had’, the third form of the verb is used. However,
‘sung’ is the third form of ‘sing’. Hence, 'I have sung' is the most
appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Mr. Suman / asked me / to pack / my luggages.
questions.explanation:
(b) my luggages.
‘Luggage’ is an uncountable noun, we cannot form its plural.
Hence, ‘my luggage’ is the most appropriate answer. (Correct)

questions.prompt: Camels tend to move slowly than other domestic animals
questions.explanation:
(c) move slowly
We use comparative degree with ‘than’ to compare two persons,
things or animals. The given sentence makes a comparison
between the movement of camels and other domestic animals.
